text.p: The Kenyan shilling held stable on Thursday, unchanged in spite of political tension which closed down Nairobi's city centre ahead of the state Budget, commercial bank dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a mean shilling rate of 55.05 against the dollar, while against the pound it was posted at a mean rate of 90.21 from 90.38.
"The market is very calm although it looks divided over the shilling's near-term direction," a dealer from a leading commercial bank said.
Demand for the dollar looked strong, mainly from oil importers, but activity could pick up on dollar inflows from foreign investors looking for treasury bills late this afternoon, dealers said.
The money market tightened slightly with overnight rates quoted at 12 percent from 10 percent on Wednesday.

Commerce came to a complete standstill on Thursday after Kenyan riot police sealed off parliament and deployed in force at strategic points around the capital to prevent a banned pro-reform demonstration on Budget day.

Dozens of police, armed with long wooden staves, shields and teargas canisters, ringed the parliament building where President Daniel arap Moi was due to hear Finance Minister Musalia Mudavadi's 1997/98 budget speech starting about 2.30 p.m. (1130 GMT).

Helmeted police patrolled Nairobi's main commercial district and men of the anti-riot General Service Unit (GSU) stood guard at strategic points. Police armed with rifles manned roadblocks on access roads into Nairobi.

The usually bustling centre of the city of three million was quiet with only a fraction of the normal pedestrian and vehicle traffic. Some city centre schools and offices were closed because of fears that pro-democracy campaigners would defy a government ban and stage a protest outside parliament.
